rationale: Romans 8:20-21 speaks of creation subjected to futility and of hope that it will be set free from bondage to decay; it restates Genesis 3:17-19's ground-level curse rather than inverting it -- the undoing is Paul's stated future hope, not something the Romans text itself accomplishes, so contrast_reversal would claim more than the text does. As a literary relation this is Paul evoking the curse without naming Genesis, which is why allusion is the more accurate type. Commentary aggregated by Precept Austin reads Romans 8:20-21 against Genesis 3:17-19 without naming a scholar; Redemptive History and Theology cites Moo (NICNT, p. 516) on the 'in hope' clause, but Moo's own page was not read and no source read here calls the reading a consensus, so the label is plausible, not strong, until a named commentator is independently verified. Genesis 3:17-19 states no promise of reversal in its own words, so promise_fulfillment would also claim more than the text supports.
